column1: # Token values per colour scheme. OKLCH throughout: it interpolates without
# the muddy midpoints hex gives you, and a lightness change stays a lightness
# change instead of quietly shifting hue.
# TOKEN NAMES are shared across every site in the family. VALUES are not, and
# must not be: two sites that look identical are two sites nobody can tell
# apart, and a shared palette means fixing one breaks the other silently.
# ORDER MATTERS. `base` rows are always emitted; the chosen theme's rows are
# emitted AFTER them, so a theme overrides base simply by restating a token.
# Keep base first in this file and never interleave.
# Anything named here can be used as a marker colour in markers.tsv.
# Named after the console, and shaped by where the pages get read: a dimmer
# room or a booth during a work call. Surfaces sit darker and cooler than base
# so a phone at full brightness is not a flashlight, and the accent is the
# amber a board op already reads as "live".
# For pages that ARE a table. Neutral, almost grey, because a coloured surface
# competes with the rows for attention -- and the rows are the content. The
# accent is used sparingly and mostly on structure, not decoration.
